newsitem.title: LEBANON: Hariri reappointment expected on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Hariri reappointment expected on Thursday.

text.p: Lebanon's President Elias Hrawi was expected to nominate Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri for a third term of office on Thursday after most parliamentary deputies called for his reappointment.
Some 101 of the 128 deputies, who were summoned on Wednesday and Thursday to the presidential palace to express their views, told reporters they had told the president they chose Hariri.
Those who did not name Hariri expressed no other choice for prime minister but said they wanted policy changes.

Hrawi, who must nominate the choice of the majority of deputies, completed his consultations before lunch and was expected to announce the nomination in the late afternoon before the arrival in Beirut of French President Jacques Chirac.

The 51-year-old Hariri, who has led a drive for national reconstruction in two previous terms of office since October 1992, is widely considered indispensable if Lebanon's postwar revival is to continue.
Political sources say the new prime minister could complete the formation of his cabinet, which needs a vote of confidence from parliament, by the end of the month.

Hariri, a construction tycoon with a personal fortune estimated at $4 billion, stepped down routinely last week after parliamentary elections to allow the new parliament to choose a new prime minister.

He is expected to have greater influence in the new parliament after winning a seat for the first time in the elections at the head of a bloc of about 20 supporters which will make him one of the strongest figures in the house.
Hariri had few supporters in the previous parliament which shelved many of his costly projects for rebuilding the country.

His new parliamentary strength, and a new political alliance with parliament Speaker Nabih Berri, with whom he frequently clashed in the old parliament, is expected to facilitate passage of his projects.

Hariri strengthened the Lebanese pound and international confidence in postwar Lebanon during his first two administrations. However, he has been accused of neglecting the poor while sinking the country into foreign debt.
He has said that the new government must make social policy a top priority.
